faqs.q: Does every Austin home need a sump pump?
faqs.a: No. Sump pumps are used where a pit collects groundwater or drainage in a low area, basement, or crawlspace. The home's layout and water history determine the need.

faqs.q: How do I test a sump pump?
faqs.a: For many systems, adding water to the pit should raise the float and start the pump. Stop and call if the pump does not start, makes unusual noise, or cannot move the water.

faqs.q: How long does a sump pump last?
faqs.a: Many pumps last roughly seven to ten years, but cycling frequency, debris, installation, and maintenance can shorten or extend that range.

faqs.q: Should I install a battery backup?
faqs.a: A backup is worth considering when the space is vulnerable to water damage or outages commonly happen during the same storms that fill the pit.

faqs.q: Can a sump pump be repaired?
faqs.a: Some float, switch, check-valve, and connection problems are repairable. A failed motor, severe corrosion, or an undersized older pump may justify replacement.

faqs.q: Why does my sump pump run all the time?
faqs.a: Common causes include a stuck switch, failed check valve, undersized pump, discharge problem, or a water source that is continuously filling the pit.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a water filter and a water softener?
faqs.a: Filtration targets specific particles, tastes, odors, or contaminants. A softener primarily exchanges hardness minerals that cause scale. Some homes benefit from one; others need both.

faqs.q: What does a whole-home water filter remove?
faqs.a: It depends on the filter media and system design. Carbon, sediment, and specialty media address different issues, so testing and a defined goal matter.

faqs.q: Do I need a water test before choosing a filter?
faqs.a: A test or reliable utility water information helps avoid guesswork, especially for wells, visible staining, unusual odors, or specific health-related concerns.

faqs.q: Is whole-home filtration better than reverse osmosis?
faqs.a: They serve different jobs. Whole-home systems treat water throughout the house; reverse osmosis is commonly used at a drinking-water tap for more targeted treatment.

faqs.q: How often do water filters need maintenance?
faqs.a: Intervals vary by media, cartridge size, water quality, and household use. We provide a schedule based on the installed system rather than a generic date.

faqs.q: Will a water filter reduce water pressure?
faqs.a: A correctly sized, maintained system should preserve useful flow. Undersized or clogged filters can restrict pressure and need correction or service.
